name: Naro Space Center
tagline: South Korea's spaceport: Naro-1 (2009-13) and the home-built Nuri rocket since 2021
description: Naro Space Center stands on the south coast of South Korea, in Goheung County about 485 km south of Seoul, and is run by KARI. It has two pads. The Naro-1 rocket, with a Russian first stage, flew from LC-1 three times: the flights of 25 August 2009 and 10 June 2010 failed to reach orbit, and on 30 January 2013 the third put the STSAT-2C satellite into low orbit. On 28 November 2018 a Nuri test vehicle flew a 10-minute suborbital hop to qualify its KRE-075 engine. Nuri, the first orbital rocket designed and built entirely in South Korea, lifted off from LC-2 on 21 October 2021 and failed in its third stage. Its second flight, on 21 June 2022, reached a 700 km orbit, and further flights followed on 25 May 2023, 26 November 2025 and 7 October 2026, all from LC-2.
